decision: All 729 fixed event-specific nearest/floor/ceil policies remain excluded as complete-year reproductions under the retained point/geometry/shared-horizon assumptions. No policy or clock model selected.
scope: Retrospective feasibility sensitivity on all 365 already exposed Istanbul 2026 days; no fresh institutional data or clock-accuracy improvement.
distribution: Counts, policy aggregates and evidence hashes only; no original calendar rows, raw epochs, derived time intervals, or per-day classification matrix.

family.astronomy: Existing own NOAA continuous geometry, not confirmed MICA
family.nonHorizonDefinitions: Fajr -19deg, Isha -17deg, true transit, Asr factor 1 with target based on transit declination
family.perDayFeasibilityRelaxation: Any common Temkin and any shared sunrise/Maghrib solar-center horizon, with no values selected as a model
family.dateInterpretation: Original printed Gregorian date and published +03 offset, consistent with Europe/Istanbul 2026; no modulo or source clock correction

limitations: Closed outer rounding cells and independent horizon-specific Temkin choices enlarge feasibility; overlap is only inconclusive, never an exact clock score.
Fixed point, own NOAA geometry, source-column meanings and shared horizon are assumptions; no MICA equivalence or publisher error claim.
Two February exclusions in the weakest cases are below 1.3 seconds and fragile to ephemeris/geometry changes. December 17 retains a larger approximately 0.109-degree shared-horizon gap.
No single day excludes all policies; the contradiction is consistency of one fixed policy over the complete year.
Old source calendars, baseline clock scores and all public numerical defaults remain unchanged.
